project.name: GDGoC AASTMT Aswan — Orientation Adventure
project.organization: Google Developer Groups on Campus — AASTMT Aswan

creative_direction.core_concept: A lost pirate map leading visitors through five technology islands, where every GDGoC track is represented as a unique explorable island.

art_style.detail_level: medium detail with strong silhouettes for mobile readability
art_style.texture: aged parchment, faded ink and subtle paper imperfections
art_style.shading: minimal watercolor washes and light cross-hatching
art_style.visual_age: old explorer map, but polished enough for a modern event identity

brand_balance.rule: Pirate theme dominates the environment while Google/GDGoC colors appear as controlled accents.
brand_balance.google_colors_usage: Never recolor the entire pirate map using Google colors. Use them only for interaction states, flags, small symbols, route markers and selected UI details.
brand_balance.logo_usage: Use official logo assets separately. Do not ask image generators to reproduce GDGoC or Google logos.
brand_balance.branding_feel: GDGoC should feel like the explorers or crew who discovered the map, not like corporate branding pasted over pirate artwork.

color_rules.google_colors: may remain relatively vivid when intentionally used as brand accents

ocean.style: illustrated map water rather than realistic sea
ocean.rule: The ocean must remain visually quieter than the islands.

islands.rule: Every island should look related but have its own silhouette and dominant landmark.

routes.width: thin but visible at mobile scale
routes.behavior: may animate as if being drawn
routes.avoid: modern navigation lines or glowing GPS trails

forbidden_differences: one island being realistic while another is illustrated
one island becoming flat vector art

typography.rule: Typography belongs to the website UI, not baked into generated island images.

display_style.use: large pirate headings and short thematic statements
display_style.limit: only decorative headings, never long paragraphs

body_style.rule: must remain easy to read on 360px mobile screens

map_labels.treatment: slightly rotated or imperfect where appropriate
map_labels.rule: implemented with real HTML/SVG text rather than generated into artwork

ui_style.philosophy: The website UI should feel physically attached to the treasure map.

border_radius.rule: do not make every element a rounded rectangle

ui_style.shadow_style: soft paper/object separation, not dramatic floating UI shadows

selected_island.effect: slight elevation and clearer ink contrast

visited_island.effect: small explorer stamp, marker or completed route indicator

rules: islands must remain recognizable when displayed around 100-170px wide
interactive targets should be at least 44px
major landmarks must remain visible at mobile scale
small decorative details must never be required for understanding
text must never be baked into island images
map should remain visually understandable without zooming

asset_generation_rules.reason: Brand assets and text should remain real frontend elements for consistency, accessibility and responsiveness.

global_negative_prompt: rectangular parchment background behind isolated assets
